sentences.text: Agujaceratops was a large dinosaur measuring about 4.3 meters in length and weighing 1.5 metric tons.
The back of its frill features a strong notch that forms a heart shape, accompanied by three or four pairs of spike-like hornlets.
Numerous low, blunt hornlets line the edges of the frill to create a strongly scalloped appearance.
The brow horns are oriented upward and outward, curving backward when viewed from the side.
Some estimates suggest the animal could reach nearly 5 meters in length, 3 meters in height, and weigh 2 tons.
Material was first found in 1938 in Big Bend National Park by William Strain.
The genus was named by Lucas, Sullivan, and Hunt in 2006.
Agujaceratops was a quadrupedal herbivore, like other ceratopsids.
The animal was originally classified under the genus Chasmosaurus before being moved to its own genus.
It lived approximately between 75 and 70 million years ago during the Campanian in what is now North America.
During this time, the Aguja Formation was located along the western margin of the Western Interior Seaway.
The habitat where fossils were found may have been a swamp, based on the nature of the sediments.
